transcript:
Header: 2026-05-01 10:00 AM UTC | Duration: 75 minutes | Attendees: Tess Kim (CEO), Ravi Patel (CTO), Maya Singh (VP Product), Jordan Brooks (Head of People), Ethan Reyes (Head of Revenue) + company-wide All Hands

Summary: Company update covering growth, runway, hiring, product milestones (Private/Dedicated), reliability investments, and go-to-market focus. Q&A at the end.

00:00:05 - Tess: Hey everyone, good morning, good afternoon, wherever you are. Thanks for joining our May all-hands. Quick note, we have about 75 minutes, we'll run through a short leadership update, product highlights, and then open for q and a.

00:00:25 - Tess: A quick housekeeping — recording is on, slides at bit.ly/rw-may-allhands, and we'll share the deck after.

00:00:45 - Tess: Before we jump in, shout out to infra for getting the new Dedicated autoscaler in beta, big win. Ethan, quick congrats?

00:00:55 - Ethan: Yeah, super proud of the team. That autoscaler is helping a few pilot customers right now, and the early numbers look promising for cost predictability.

00:01:15 - Tess: Cool. Alright, I'll start with company metrics. High level first. Revenue: month-over-month ARR growth sits at 6% for April, and net retention ticked up to 112%. Pipeline is healthy for mid-market and enterprise.

00:01:38 - Tess: Cash runway, we've extended runway slightly due to cost controls and the Dedicated pilot revenue; we now forecast runway to mid-2027 under current plan. We're still keeping a conservative approach to hiring but we'll re-open prioritized roles — Jordan will cover details.

00:01:58 - Jordan: Thanks. Quick recap on hiring: we had a temporary freeze in March, we've prioritized customer-facing and infra roles. Today we are approving 18 new reqs across infra, reliability, and sales. The People team will publish the updated headcount plan and timeline this week. We are balancing speed and comp discipline.

00:02:22 - Maya: Question from product — is engineering capacity prioritized for Private deployments or for general hosted performance improvements?

00:02:31 - Tess: Short answer: both, but Private + Dedicated get weight this quarter because we see enterprise demand tied to compliance and long-term contracts. There's also a backlog of performance work that improves unit economics across all customers.

00:02:50 - Ravi: I'll add a bit more technical color. On the runtime side, we shipped the KV caching improvements last month — though the telemetry shows a couple of edge cases with long prompt chains where cache invalidation was a bit noisy. We're patching that; the fix is in staging and we'll deploy next week. Also, we're standardizing profiling to pick better kernels for 4k token workloads.

00:03:20 - Speaker 5: (inaudible) - did you say K-V cash?

00:03:25 - Ravi: (laughs) KV cache, yeah, sorry. The auto-transcribe seems to like 'cash' sometimes.

00:03:35 - Tess: On product roadmap: Maya?

00:03:40 - Maya: Thanks. High level milestones for Q2: 1) Private deployment GA alpha for one regulated customer; 2) rollout of improved autoscaling UI in Console; 3) Optimize features — batching suggestions and quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize — will reach beta. We're also piloting a focused eval program so customers can run quality checks before rolling out model updates.

00:04:10 - Maya: For Private specifically, we're focused on onboarding simplicity — a one-day bootstrap for VPC customers and clearer docs for KMS/HSM integrations. We know audits have long lead times so we're investing in compliance artifacts.

00:04:34 - Tess: Thanks Maya. A couple of operational notes: we'll be increasing observability retention for core endpoints for 30 days to help debugging and regressions; that will be opt-in for low-tier accounts due to cost.

00:04:52 - Ethan: On go-to-market: pipeline is expanding in North America and we're seeing early traction in EMEA. For Dedicated, the pilot pricing is close to final — we'll share a playbook for SDRs and AEs next week. We're also working on a targeted pilot for ISVs who need predictable unit economics.

00:05:15 - Ethan: A thing to flag — a few prospects asked about SOC 2 type II and regional data residency. We have SOC 2 in progress and the compliance team is drafting residency options for EU customers.

00:05:35 - Tess: Good point. Security/compliance is a blocker for some deals; Ravi, maybe say a few words about our roadmap here?

00:05:40 - Ravi: Sure. SOC 2 audit kickoff is this month. For data residency, the short-term plan is to offer region-specific endpoints in partnership with cloud providers; longer-term we have Private packages that let customers keep data in their VPCs. We're also adding more audit log granularity and SSO/SAML improvements.

00:06:05 - Tess: Great. Ok let's move to engineering highlights — Ravi will run through a quick tech update.

00:06:12 - Ravi: Thanks. Key things: kernel selector improvements, KV cache fixes, continuous batching improvements, and some quantization experiments that are showing 2-3x inference cost reduction on select models without large quality regressions. We're careful about regression alerts — Maya's team will own the eval gating.

00:06:38 - Ravi: Also, the Dedicated autoscaler that Ethan mentioned — we implemented backpressure routing and fallback to smaller model variants when capacity is constrained. Early pilots saw 15% lower tail latency for web use cases.

00:06:58 - Speaker 7: Quick question — are we open-sourcing any of the runtime improvements?

00:07:02 - Ravi: Some parts yes. We'll open-source helper libs and docs, but low-level kernel tuning and infra choices will stay internal for now. We want to keep a competitive advantage on serving efficiency.

00:07:20 - Tess: Ok back to company metrics for a moment — a couple of items to call out: CAC has improved slightly since we streamlined the self-serve onboarding and free credits flow; gross margin on hosted API is up because of caching and batching gains. We're not out of the woods but trajectory is positive.

00:07:45 - Tess: Hiring priorities: infra reliability, SRE, and a few senior sales hires for enterprise. We also approved a small headcount for Developer Experience — docs and quickstarts — which should help PLG.

00:08:00 - Jordan: On benefits and culture — we're re-opening the remote work stipends and will run an all-company offsite in September. Also, People team is updating the parental leave policy to be more flexible; details coming next week.

00:08:20 - Tess: Great. Now let's open the Q&A. Please use the Q&A form in the slides or raise your hand.

00:08:38 - Speaker 12 (Engineering): Question — for Private GA, what does success look like and what's the target customer profile?

00:08:46 - Maya: Success is threefold: 1) customer can deploy a model in their VPC with our control plane in under a week; 2) we have observability and audit logs that satisfy common security reviews; 3) we convert at least 30% of pilots to paid contracts within 90 days. Target customers are regulated mid-market and enterprise in finance, healthcare, and edtech.

00:09:15 - Speaker 14 (Sales): Question — for Dedicated pricing, will we have a standard playbook or is it going to be custom?

00:09:22 - Ethan: There will be a standard pricing band for typical Dedicated commits and add-ons for higher availability and longer retention. We still expect some negotiation for large enterprise deals. We'll publish the playbook and example SOW templates next week.

00:09:40 - Speaker 18 (Product): Clarification — the eval gating Maya mentioned, will that be automated or manual?

00:09:46 - Maya: The plan is automated pre-deploy evals tied to a prompt set; manual review for significant model upgrades or customers with strict quality requirements. We'll provide an interface in Console for customers to run their own evals.

00:10:03 - Tess: Ok couple more quick items then we'll wrap. We're launching a monthly performance sprint — cross-functional engineering and product focused on latency and unit-cost wins. First sprint starts next week.

00:10:20 - Tess: Also, reminder — leadership office hours next Friday for deeper questions and follow-ups. And we'll have breakout lunches by function the following week.

00:10:35 - Q&A continues with a mix of product, security, and people questions. Transcription below includes representative snippets and timestamps; some names or terms may be slightly off due to auto-transcribe.

00:12:00 - Speaker 23 (Sales): Are we reprioritizing roadmap items to chase short-term revenue?

00:12:07 - Tess: We're balancing. We won't sacrifice long-term platform health, but we will accelerate work that unlocks enterprise contracts — Private, Dedicated, and compliance artifacts.

00:12:30 - Speaker 25 (Engineering): Any change to on-call rota with the new infra hires?

00:12:36 - Jordan: We'll publish the updated on-call schedule once hiring is filled; for now keep current rota but expect small shifts.

00:13:00 - Speaker 27 (Finance): Quick question — can you confirm runway guidance again?

00:13:06 - Tess: Yes, with current plans and modest revenue from Dedicated pilots, runway is mid-2027. That assumes conservative hiring and some upside from enterprise conversions.

00:13:30 - Speaker 29 (New hire): Where can I find docs to get up to speed with the runtime?

00:13:35 - Ravi: We'll share a curated onboarding playbook in the docs site and link from the slides. Also reach out on #runtime-onboarding channel.

00:14:00 - Tess: Ok wrapping up — quick recap of next steps and action items. We'll share slides, People will publish headcount plan, Ravi will circulate Private benchmarks, Maya will update the product roadmap. Thank you everyone.

00:14:20 - Tess: One last thing — appreciation for shipping stuff, small wins add up. See you at office hours.

00:14:30 - Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcribe picked up some words incorrectly (e.g., 'K-V cash' instead of 'KV cache'), speaker attribution is coarse in places, and some short crosstalk is not perfectly separated.
